agenda: The situation concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo; Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (S/2025/779)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France aims to renew MONUSCO with a protection-forward, conditions-based mandate that supports the Washington, Doha, Luanda and Nairobi processes while pressing M23 and external forces to withdraw and preserving humanitarian access. The main difficulties will be the duration and scope of the extension, the strength of language attributing support to M23, and balancing DRC sovereignty concerns with the need to avoid security gaps. We expect broad support but may need to calibrate explicit attribution and withdrawal benchmarks to preserve Council unity.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's core objectives, especially the conditions-based extension of MONUSCO, protection of civilians and the demand for withdrawal of M23 and external forces. We ask the penholder to strengthen African ownership by adding a preambular reference to the African Union Peace and Security Council statement of 14 February 2025 and the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, and by reordering OP8 to foreground African-led mediation. We also request that OP2 expressly recall the consent of the Government of the DRC and the comprehensive disengagement plan. With these adjustments Algeria can join consensus.
messages.China: China supports the draft and welcomes the DRC–Rwanda peace agreement and M23's announced withdrawal from Uvira. We suggest clarifying OP5 to refer to unauthorized external forces and to link withdrawal to the relevant peace agreements and verification mechanisms, so as to uphold the consent principle and avoid prejudicing legitimate bilateral security cooperation. We also encourage the Council to stress full implementation of regional processes under African ownership.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft’s robust focus on protection of civilians, conditions-based withdrawal and condemnation of external support to M23. We ask for two targeted strengthenings: human rights vetting and international law compliance for support to DRC security forces in OP12, and explicit reporting on WPS/YPS, child protection and climate-related security risks in OP13. With these changes, Denmark is ready to support the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft as a strong basis and welcomes the penholder's balanced text. We ask that support to DRC defence and security forces be explicitly conditioned on full compliance with international law and the sanctions regime, and that OP9 explicitly include United Nations personnel and peacekeepers among those to be protected. Greece remains ready to support the text once these refinements are reflected.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a strong basis and thanks France for its penholdership. We ask for targeted additions to ensure that support to security forces includes human rights and accountability safeguards and that regional peace efforts explicitly reflect the decisions of the African Union Peace and Security Council. We would also welcome language on durable solutions for internally displaced persons and refugees, consistent with Guyana’s humanitarian priorities.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of MONUSCO's mandate and the draft's emphasis on sovereignty, protection of civilians and regional peace processes. We ask that the text retain the Council's previously agreed neutral formulation on external forces rather than singling out a neighbouring State, and that it expressly address the safety and security of peacekeepers. We also seek a modest addition on tracking financial resources linked to illicit natural-resource exploitation, consistent with Pakistan's long-standing position.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the penholder’s balanced text, which reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, MONUSCO’s protection-of-civilians role, and the demand for M23 and external forces to withdraw. We would ask for a few refinements: explicit host-State consent in the conditions-based approach, human rights and accountability safeguards for support to DRC security forces, and recognition of Ituri among threatened areas requiring protection. We can support the text with these changes and would oppose any weakening of these points.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the penholder’s balanced and comprehensive text and supports its adoption. We ask for refinements to ensure that any support to the DRC’s defence and security forces is explicitly conditioned on compliance with international law and the arms embargo, that peacekeepers and accountability for attacks on United Nations personnel are clearly covered, and that external-force withdrawal is tied to agreed regional verification mechanisms. These changes would strengthen implementation and preserve Council unity.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of MONUSCO and the draft's emphasis on implementing the Washington, Doha and Luanda processes. We ask that attribution of external support be handled carefully and through agreed verification mechanisms, and that withdrawal demands be tied to those mechanisms and timelines rather than presented as an immediate ultimatum. We also believe African-led mediation should be given due prominence and MONUSCO's conditions-based withdrawal should be explicitly linked to the consent and priorities of the Government of the DRC. With these balanced adjustments, we can support the resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as a strong basis and welcomes its focus on protection of civilians, conditions-based withdrawal and full implementation of the peace agreements. We ask the penholder to anchor implementation more explicitly in African-led regional processes by referring to the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes in OP7 and by including the East African Community and the Economic Community of Central African States in OP8. We also suggest adding language on safe, voluntary and dignified return and reintegration of IDPs and refugees, consistent with resolution 2765 (2024).
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the balanced draft and can support the renewal of MONUSCO's mandate. We ask for refinements to anchor the conditions-based approach in consultation with local communities, to explicitly require freedom of movement and cooperation with MONUSCO, and to strengthen survivor-centred accountability and reporting on climate-related security risks. We also propose adding durable solutions for internally displaced persons and refugees in OP12.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of MONUSCO and the conditions-based approach in the text, and thanks the penholder for incorporating the DRC–Rwanda and regional processes. As an African member, we ask that the draft explicitly anchor the Council’s support in the African Common Position and foreground African-led mediation, including Angola, the AU, ICGLR and SADC. We also suggest practical reference to agreed regional verification and liaison mechanisms in OP5 so that demands are implementable and do not complicate ongoing peace efforts. We are ready to work constructively for consensus.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes and broadly supports the French draft, which captures the need for M23 withdrawal, Rwandan withdrawal and a conditions-based MONUSCO approach. We ask that OP4 and OP5 be strengthened to require verifiable withdrawal from all occupied areas and an explicit cessation of Rwandan military support to M23. We also seek a new operative paragraph demanding full cooperation with, and protection of, MONUSCO personnel. Subject to those changes, we are ready to support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft and thanks France for its leadership. We need the text to name the Rwanda Defence Force directly, as the Group of Experts has documented, rather than rely on euphemisms. We also seek urgent 1533 Committee action on designations, verification of M23's announced withdrawal, and human rights vetting for any security-sector support.

replies.Denmark: accepted: human rights vetting and expanded reporting included.
replies.Greece: accepted: sanctions compliance and protection of United Nations personnel and peacekeepers included.
replies.Guyana: accepted: AU Peace and Security Council decisions, safeguards, and durable solutions for IDPs and refugees included.
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: safety of MONUSCO personnel and financial-resource tracking included; neutral external-forces formulation not fully retained.
replies.Panama: accepted: host-State consent, safeguards, and Ituri reference included.
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: verification mechanisms, peacekeeper protections, and arms-embargo compliance included.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: verification, Government priorities, and African ownership included; explicit RDF attribution and immediate withdrawal retained.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, EAC and ECCAS, and IDP and refugee return language included.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: community consultation, MONUSCO cooperation, survivor-centred services, IDP return, and climate reporting included.
replies.Somalia: accepted: African Common Position, African-led mediation, and verification mechanisms included.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: verifiable M23 and RDF withdrawal, cessation of Rwandan support, and MONUSCO protection paragraph included.
replies.United States of America: accepted: RDF named, 1533 Committee designations, verification, and vetting included.

steps.summary: The revision bridges US and UK red lines by naming the Rwanda Defence Force and requiring verifiable withdrawal, while incorporating African-led mediation, host-State consent, human rights safeguards, and durable solutions for displaced persons. The text is expected to attract broad support, with China, Russia, and Pakistan likely abstaining rather than vetoing.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating the African Union Peace and Security Council language, the centrality of African-led mediation, and the consent of the Government of the DRC. We believe the text now reflects the need for a political solution within the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC. Algeria calls on all Council members to unite and adopt the text without delay.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder’s efforts and supports in principle the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate and the emphasis on African-led and regional processes. To maintain balance and respect the parties’ peace commitments, OP6 should be aligned with the relevant peace agreements and verification mechanisms rather than demanding an unconditional withdrawal. We also ask that OP13 designations be evidence-based and follow established procedures. With these adjustments, China is prepared to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on human rights vetting and expanded reporting. The current text reflects the balance needed on protection of civilians, accountability, humanitarian access, WPS/YPS, child protection and climate-related security risks. Denmark supports the draft as it stands and looks forward to its adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft as a balanced and credible basis for Council action. We welcome the incorporation of our points on full compliance with international law and the sanctions regime, and on the protection of United Nations personnel and peacekeepers. Greece encourages all members to unite behind the text and to focus on its full and expeditious implementation, including respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and a conditions-based MONUSCO withdrawal. No further changes are requested.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised text and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier requests, including the reference to relevant African Union Peace and Security Council decisions, safeguards on support to security forces, and durable solutions for IDPs and refugees. The draft maintains a clear focus on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and African-led mediation. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and urge full implementation of the Washington, Doha and Luanda/Nairobi processes. Guyana is ready to vote in favour of the text as it stands.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate and welcomes the inclusion of language on the safety and security of MONUSCO personnel and on tracking financial resources linked to the illicit exploitation of natural resources. We remain concerned, however, that singling out a neighbouring State by name risks complicating the Washington, Doha and Luanda processes, and we therefore ask that the established neutral formulation on external forces be restored and that verification be anchored in the agreed regional mechanisms. Pakistan can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder for incorporating its requests on host-State consent, human rights and accountability safeguards, and the reference to Ituri. The current text reflects Panama’s priorities: the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, protection of civilians, support for MONUSCO, and a political solution through regional processes. Panama therefore supports the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks France for incorporating our earlier proposals on verification mechanisms, peacekeeper protection and arms-embargo compliance. We support the revised text and encourage all Council members to unite behind it. Full implementation of the Washington, Doha and Luanda processes, safe humanitarian access and accountability remain essential, and we will vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the inclusion of verification through agreed regional mechanisms, respect for the Government of the DRC’s priorities and African-led ownership. We can support the text if OP6 and PP10 are aligned with the Washington, Doha and Luanda processes by referring to agreed timelines and verified reporting, rather than prescribing immediate and unconditional withdrawal or prejudging attribution. We also ask for standard evidentiary safeguards for any Committee designations.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the incorporation of the merged Luanda–Nairobi process, EAC and ECCAS, and IDP and refugee return language, and supports the balanced text. We ask only that OP7 be aligned with OP8 by referring to the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes rather than listing them separately, consistent with the African Common Position. Sierra Leone is ready to vote in favour once this textual consistency is addressed.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on community consultation, MONUSCO cooperation, survivor-centred services, IDP return and climate reporting. We believe the draft strikes the right balance between a conditions-based MONUSCO presence, protection of civilians and accountability for violations. We have no further changes and encourage the Council to send a unified message.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating the African Common Position, African-led mediation and regional verification mechanisms. The text provides a balanced basis for protecting civilians, supporting MONUSCO’s conditions-based mandate and advancing African-led peace efforts in the DRC and the Great Lakes region. We will vote in favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the revised text and welcomes the inclusion of verifiable withdrawal of M23 and Rwandan forces, cessation of Rwandan support to M23, and strengthened MONUSCO protection language. We encourage all Council members to support adoption and call for the full and urgent implementation of this resolution.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised text and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our core concerns, including naming the Rwanda Defence Force and advancing 1533 Committee designations. We still need OP6 to demand, not merely call upon, that Rwanda immediately cease all military support to M23; this is essential to reflect the gravity of the Group of Experts’ findings and to maintain credible accountability.

replies.China: partially accepted: OP6 no longer unconditional and OP13 includes evidentiary safeguards; immediate withdrawal reference adjusted
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: PP softened to grave concern at reports and verification stressed; Rwanda remains named in OP6
replies.Russian Federation: accepted: OP6 aligned with agreed timelines and verification, PP reworded to grave concern at reports, and OP13 safeguards added
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: OP6 now refers to the Doha process and merged Luanda and Nairobi processes
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP6 now demands that Rwanda immediately cease all military support to M23

steps.summary: France as penholder revised OP6 to demand Rwanda cease support while aligning force withdrawal with agreed timelines and verification, softened the relevant preambular paragraph to grave concern at reports, and added evidentiary safeguards for 1533 Committee designations. The text retains strong MONUSCO protection, sovereignty, humanitarian and sanctions language and is expected to attract broad support with Pakistan abstaining.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria had expressed support and requested no changes; voting in favour is consistent with its record of backing consensus resolutions, African-led processes, sovereignty, and protection of civilians in the DRC.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported MONUSCO mandate renewals and a political settlement in the DRC, and its key textual concerns were partially addressed. Voting in favour is consistent with China’s support for peacekeeping and African-led regional processes while avoiding a veto on a broadly supported text.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark has consistently supported MONUSCO and the France-penned DRC text, and the draft aligns with Danish priorities on civilian protection, international law, and regional peace processes. It made no requested changes and voted in favour in the last negotiation round.
reasons.France: France authored the draft and has consistently supported MONUSCO mandate renewal, protection of civilians, and firm language on M23 and unauthorized foreign forces. It would speak before the vote as penholder to present the text and urge Council unity.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported MONUSCO mandate renewals and voted in favour of the prior DRC resolutions, and this draft aligns with its emphasis on sovereignty, humanitarian access, regional peace processes and protection of civilians.
reasons.Guyana: The draft aligns with Guyana’s consistent support for DRC sovereignty, civilian protection, African-led mediation and previous Council resolutions on MONUSCO and the region. Guyana requested no changes and is expected to vote in favour while explaining key priorities before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported DRC/MONUSCO resolutions and Council consensus; despite its OP6 wording request not being fully met, the draft advances peacekeeping, protection of civilians and regional processes, so Pakistan would vote yes with an explanatory statement.
reasons.Panama: Panama supported the draft in negotiations without requesting changes and has consistently backed MONUSCO, DRC sovereignty, and regional peace processes. Voting in favour aligns with its stated foreign policy and prior votes on this agenda item.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supported the draft in the last negotiation round and has consistently voted for MONUSCO and DRC-related resolutions. A yes vote aligns with Seoul’s support for UN peacekeeping, sovereignty, humanitarian access, and African-led peace processes.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently supported previous DRC/MONUSCO resolutions and its key amendments were accepted, including verification-based language and sanctions safeguards. Voting in favour preserves its support for African-led processes while allowing it to register caveats on unverified allegations.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone’s requested alignment of OP6 was accepted, and the draft reflects its priorities of African-led peace processes, protection of civilians, and a conditions-based MONUSCO mandate. Sierra Leone therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia had already expressed support and the draft reflects its priorities on protection of civilians, human rights, WPS, and multilateral implementation of peace agreements. As an elected member with a consistent record of voting in favour on this file, Slovenia would support the French penholder text.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia’s established position supports African-led mediation, DRC sovereignty, MONUSCO and the France-penholder resolutions; it requested no changes and is expected to vote in favour.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK’s last-round position was support with no requested changes, and the draft aligns with UK policy on MONUSCO, DRC sovereignty, M23 withdrawal, humanitarian access, and implementation of African-led and other peace processes. The UK would therefore vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports the resolution, and its key requested change strengthening OP6 was accepted. Voting in favour advances U.S. policy on MONUSCO renewal, M23 withdrawal, and accountability for Rwandan support to M23.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholder for the inclusive consultations and welcome the Council’s continued unity on the situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Algeria supports the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate in a phased, flexible and conditions-based manner, with full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and consent of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the basic principles of peacekeeping. We stress that there can be no military solution to this crisis. We therefore call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the full and verifiable withdrawal of M23 and all unauthorized external forces from Congolese territory, and the faithful implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda and Nairobi processes. Algeria reaffirms the centrality of African-led mediation and regional ownership, including by the African Union, Angola, the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region, SADC, the East African Community and ECCAS. We underscore the urgency of safe, unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, including women and children, and we call on all parties to comply fully with international humanitarian law and human rights law and to ensure accountability for violations. My delegation will remain engaged to support a political settlement that safeguards the sovereignty and stability of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the wider Great Lakes region.
before.China:
Mr President,

China thanks the penholder for its efforts and the constructive engagement on this draft. The situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remains complex and fragile. China has consistently supported the role of MONUSCO in promoting security and stability in the DRC, and we support the extension of its mandate under conditions-based and phased arrangements, with the consent of and in close coordination with the Government of the DRC, so as to avoid creating security gaps.

China believes that there is no military solution to the conflict in the eastern DRC. The peace process is at a critical juncture, and the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all regional States must be fully respected. We welcome the recent regional and international mediation efforts, including the Washington agreement, the Doha process and the Regional Economic Integration Framework, and encourage the DRC and Rwanda to implement these commitments in good faith and resolve their differences through dialogue. All parties should cease hostilities, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. The withdrawal of unauthorized external forces and the cessation of military support to armed groups should be implemented and verified through the agreed regional mechanisms. We also note the revisions made to strengthen verification and evidentiary safeguards in the text. On this basis, China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We strongly support MONUSCO’s continued role in protecting civilians and welcome the conditions-based approach to its mandate and withdrawal. Denmark underscores the need for the immediate and verifiable withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, the cessation of all external military support to armed groups, full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also stress that accountability for human rights violations and international humanitarian law violations, including conflict-related sexual violence and violations against children, must remain central, and that the Washington, Doha and Luanda/Nairobi processes must be implemented fully and in good faith.
before.France: Thank you, Mr. President. France will vote in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted. The text conveys a clear and balanced message: there can be no military solution in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC must be respected; M23 must immediately cease its offensives and withdraw from all occupied areas, including Uvira and Sange; and all unauthorized external forces, including as reported the Rwanda Defence Force, must withdraw and all military support to M23 must cease. The draft also calls for full implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda–Nairobi processes, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability, and the effective implementation of the sanctions regime. It extends MONUSCO through a phased, flexible and conditions-based approach that avoids security gaps and prioritizes protection of civilians. France welcomes African-led mediation and the efforts of the United States, Qatar and the United Nations. We call on all members to support this text so that the Council speaks with one voice in support of peace in the Great Lakes region.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this resolution. We support the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate through a conditions-based and phased approach, with clear priority for the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access. We also stress the need for full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the immediate and verifiable withdrawal of M23 and unauthorized external forces, and the full implementation of the Washington, Doha and Luanda/Nairobi processes. Greece remains firmly committed to accountability, the protection of children, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in peace efforts.
before.Guyana: Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the French delegation for its leadership and for the inclusive consultations that have brought us to this point. Guyana remains steadfast in its support for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region. We call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the full and verifiable withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, including Uvira and Sange, and the withdrawal of all unauthorized external forces in accordance with agreed regional mechanisms. Guyana emphasizes the centrality of African-led and regionally owned mediation, and we urge the parties to implement fully and in good faith the Washington, Doha, Luanda and Nairobi processes. We also underscore the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and ensuring that MONUSCO’s withdrawal remains conditions-based and avoids creating security gaps. Guyana will continue to work with all Council members to support peace and stability in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Great Lakes region.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks France for its facilitation and supports the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate through a phased, conditions-based approach that prioritizes the protection of civilians and avoids security gaps. We welcome the regional and bilateral peace processes and stress the need for their full implementation. At the same time, Pakistan has consistently held that reports of external military support should be verified through the agreed regional mechanisms and that the Council’s language should avoid prejudging such matters. While our preferred formulation in operative paragraph 6 was not fully reflected, we will vote in favour of the draft as a whole in the interest of peace, stability and the protection of civilians in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. Panama supports the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate through a phased, flexible and conditions-based approach, with priority given to the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, human rights monitoring and support for the implementation of peace agreements. There can be no military solution to this conflict. We call on M23 and all armed groups to cease hostilities and withdraw from occupied areas, on all unauthorized external forces to withdraw from Congolese territory, and on all parties to implement fully the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda and Nairobi processes. We also stress the importance of African-led mediation, accountability for serious violations, and the protection of children, women and humanitarian personnel. Panama remains committed to a peaceful, negotiated and inclusive solution for the DRC and the Great Lakes region.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate through a phased, flexible and conditions-based approach, with clear priority for the protection of civilians and safe, unhindered humanitarian access. The situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo requires urgent implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, the immediate and verifiable withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas, and the full withdrawal of all unauthorized external forces consistent with the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC. We also stress the importance of African-led mediation, accountability for serious violations, and the full participation of women and youth in peace processes. We urge all parties to cease hostilities and cooperate fully with MONUSCO and humanitarian actors.
before.Russian Federation: Mr President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We believe that it responds to the need to support the peace process, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the conditions-based implementation of MONUSCO’s mandate. We note that the penholder took into account a number of our proposals, including language on verification through the agreed regional mechanisms and on the need for sanctions-related decisions to be based on sufficient evidence and the Committee’s guidelines. We stress that reports concerning external support to armed groups must be verified through the agreed regional mechanisms and should not be used to prejudge the outcome of the political process. The primary path to settlement is the full implementation by all parties of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda–Nairobi processes and African-led mediation. We call on the DRC and Rwanda to implement their commitments in good faith and without delay.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank France for its continued leadership and for accepting our proposed adjustment to operative paragraph 6, which now aligns the text with the Doha process and the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes and reflects the African-led approach that Sierra Leone has consistently supported. Sierra Leone remains deeply concerned by the continued offensive by M23, the unauthorized presence of external forces, and the grave humanitarian and human rights situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. We support the conditions-based extension of MONUSCO’s mandate, including its role in protecting civilians, facilitating humanitarian access, and supporting verification of withdrawals. We call on all parties, including M23 and all external forces, to implement fully the Washington, Doha, and merged Luanda and Nairobi commitments, cease hostilities, withdraw from occupied areas, end support to armed groups, and ensure accountability. Our vote reflects our commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and to African-led solutions.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of MONUSCO’s mandate through a conditions-based and flexible approach, with clear priority for the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the full implementation of the Washington, Doha and Luanda/Nairobi processes. We reiterate the need for all parties to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, ensure accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, protect children and survivors of conflict-related sexual violence, and guarantee the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in peace and political processes.
before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. We support the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the full and verifiable withdrawal of unauthorized external forces and armed groups from Congolese territory. As an African member of this Council, we stress the centrality of African-led and regionally owned mediation, including the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, the Doha process and the efforts of Angola and the African Union. We value the resolution’s support for MONUSCO’s conditions-based role and for the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. Somalia encourages all parties to honour their commitments, pursue dialogue and implement agreed peace and verification mechanisms in good faith.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank France for its leadership as penholder and for producing a balanced text that renews MONUSCO’s mandate on a conditions-based basis while keeping the protection of civilians at its core. The United Kingdom strongly supports the demand for the immediate, full and verifiable withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, including Uvira and Sange, and for the withdrawal of all unauthorized external forces from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, consistent with its sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also underline the importance of full implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda and Nairobi processes, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. The United Kingdom urges all parties to cooperate fully with MONUSCO and to comply with their obligations under this resolution and international law.
before.United States of America: The United States welcomes this resolution and will vote in favour. It reflects the gravity of the situation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and the urgent need for M23’s immediate, full and verifiable withdrawal, including from Uvira and Sange, and for Rwanda to cease all military support to M23. We welcome the change in operative paragraph 6 to demand—not merely call upon—Rwanda to cease such support. We also stress that MONUSCO’s conditions-based withdrawal must be coordinated with the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and must not create security gaps. The protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for violations, and full implementation of the Washington and Doha processes must remain at the centre of the Council’s efforts. The United States remains prepared to consider further measures, including through the sanctions Committee, against those who continue to destabilize the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

after.France: Thank you, Mr. President. France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and thanks all members of the Council for their constructive engagement. The Council has sent a clear and balanced message: there can be no military solution to the conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and of all States in the region must be fully respected; M23 must immediately cease its offensives and withdraw fully and verifiably from all occupied areas, including Uvira and Sange; and all unauthorized external forces, including the Rwandan forces as reported, must withdraw, while all military support to M23 must cease. The resolution also calls for the full and good-faith implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda–Nairobi processes, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law. France remains fully mobilized to support these efforts, including the conditions-based extension of MONUSCO’s mandate, so that the Mission can continue to protect civilians and accompany the restoration of State authority, in close coordination with the Congolese Government and regional partners.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We thank France for its leadership as penholder and for the balanced and inclusive text, and we thank all Council members for their constructive engagement.

The adoption of this resolution must now be translated into concrete action. Panama reiterates its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. We call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the full and verifiable withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, including Uvira and Sange, and the withdrawal of all unauthorized external forces from Congolese territory. We also stress the need for full and good-faith implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda–Nairobi processes.

Panama supports MONUSCO’s conditions-based mandate, with protection of civilians at its core, and underscores the importance of safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in peace efforts. We urge all parties to comply with their obligations under international law and with the commitments they have undertaken.

Thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of MONUSCO. We supported it because it preserves the central role of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the principles of consent and conditions-based withdrawal, and the priority of African-led mediation.

We note that the penholder took into account our proposals regarding verification through the agreed regional mechanisms and the need for sanctions-related decisions to be based on sufficient evidence and the Committee’s guidelines. We stress once again that reports of external support to armed groups must be verified through those mechanisms and must not be used to prejudge the political process or to exert unilateral pressure.

The key task now is the faithful implementation of the Washington, Doha and merged Luanda–Nairobi agreements. We call on all parties to cease hostilities, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region. MONUSCO’s phased withdrawal must be coordinated with the Congolese authorities and must not create security gaps.

Russia will continue to support the settlement of the situation in the eastern DRC through political and diplomatic means.
